newsitem.title: FINLAND: Yeltsin to defend Russian interests more than ever.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to defend Russian interests more than ever.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin will represent Moscow's interests "like never before" at the summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton starting on Thursday, Yeltsin's spokesman said.

Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told reporters: "The president is ready to defend Russia's national interests firmly like never before." But he added it was still possible to achieve results from the two-day summit.
"It is not the goal of the summit to reach some concrete and definite agreement," Yastrzhembsky added.

"The main task of the summit in this topic (NATO) is to reach the highest level of mutual understanding to understand better the concerns and preoccupations of Russia and to understand better the reasons of the American decision on NATO expansion."

The Kremlin spokesman -- with a captive audience of around 2,000 journalists in Helsinki for the summit -- has launched a one-man public relations attack against NATO's plans to expand the alliance towards the east, even before his president arrives.
Asked if he was pessimistic about the Helsinki summit, Yastrzhembsky replied: "You can start from low expectations and get results."
